title: Buffalo Bills vs. New York Jets Live Score & Stats – November 15, 2026 Update on CBS Sports Gametracker
body:
Buffalo’s quarterback Josh Allen delivered a career‑defining performance on Tuesday night, propelling the Bills to a 38‑21 victory over the New York Jets and cementing the team’s most impressive start in three and a half decades. Allen’s dual‑threat display—racking up 312 passing yards, three touchdowns, and a 45‑yard scramble for a fourth score—ignited the Buffalo offense early and kept New York’s defense on its heels for the entire contest. The win not only improved the Bills to 5‑0, but also sparked a surge of optimism among fans and analysts who have long awaited a return to the dominance the franchise enjoyed in the early 1990s.

The Bills’ early momentum was evident from the opening drive, when Allen orchestrated a methodical 12‑play march that culminated in a 22‑yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Stefon Diggs. The connection, now in its third season, appeared more telepathic than ever, with Diggs exploiting mismatches against the Jets’ secondary. By the end of the first quarter, Buffalo had already amassed 14 points, while the Jets struggled to generate any sustained offense, managing only a field goal after a three‑and‑out series. The Bills’ aggressive play‑calling, featuring a blend of quick slants, deep posts, and occasional rollouts, forced New York’s linebackers to hesitate, opening lanes for Allen’s occasional runs.

New York attempted a comeback in the second quarter, leveraging a short‑yardage rushing attack anchored by Breece Hall, who broke off a 12‑yard touchdown run to narrow the deficit to 21‑10. However, the Bills responded with a swift 68‑yard drive highlighted by a 31‑yard strike to rookie tight end Dalton Kincaid, who displayed poise beyond his years. Allen capped the drive with a 5‑yard touchdown scramble, showcasing his ability to extend plays when the pocket collapsed. The Jets’ defense, which had shown flashes of resilience earlier in the season, appeared outmatched by Buffalo’s balanced attack and the relentless pressure generated by the Bills’ defensive line, led by star edge rusher Von Miller.

Defensively, Buffalo’s unit forced three turnovers—two interceptions by safety Jordan Poyer and a fumble recovery by defensive end Gregory Rousseau—each of which translated into points on the board. The Bills’ secondary, often criticized for inconsistency, displayed disciplined coverage, limiting the Jets’ passing game to a modest 180 yards. Meanwhile, the Jets’ offense, led by veteran quarterback Zach Wilson, sputtered under pressure, completing just 55 percent of his passes and throwing one interception that was returned deep into New York territory. Wilson’s inability to establish a rhythm was compounded by an offensive line that struggled to contain Allen’s occasional blitzes, resulting in a sack‑heavy night for the visiting quarterback.

The victory also carries significant implications for the AFC East race. With the Bills now perched atop the division, they have widened the gap on the Miami Dolphins, who sit a game behind after a narrow win over the Patriots. Buffalo’s surge is anchored not only in Allen’s elite play but also in the emergence of a cohesive supporting cast: Diggs remains a top‑10 receiver league‑wide, Kincaid provides a reliable red‑zone target, and the offensive line, bolstered by the addition of veteran guard Kevin Zeitler, has markedly reduced sacks compared with last season. If the Bills can maintain this level of execution, they are poised to challenge the Kansas City Chiefs for the AFC’s top seed.

Looking ahead, Buffalo’s next test comes against the Baltimore Ravens, a team renowned for its physicality and disciplined defense. Analysts will be watching to see whether Allen can replicate his dual‑threat performance against a unit that excels at pressuring quarterbacks. Moreover, the Bills must ensure that their defensive success is not a one‑off; sustaining turnover generation against high‑caliber opponents will be essential. Should they continue their upward trajectory, the Bills could very well rewrite the narrative of their franchise’s recent history, turning a 35‑year drought of early‑season dominance into a realistic championship pursuit.
